sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, and risk generally increases as the share of the credit limit in use rises.
Its effect is sharpest above about 72% utilization, where the model's contribution to default risk rises much more steeply than at lower levels.
Past delinquencies are the second or third most important driver: having any delinquency on file raises default risk compared with having none.
Income is also among the top three drivers, and higher income generally lowers default risk.
Length of credit history has at most a weak effect, with longer histories generally associated with lower risk.
The effect of utilization grows with past delinquencies, so the combination of high utilization and delinquencies is especially risky.
Debt-to-income ratio has at most a weak effect, and the data do not settle whether it increases default risk.
Age, number of dependents, months at address and recent credit inquiries hardly matter for the model's predictions.
